export { Autocomplete } from "./Autocomplete";
export type { AutocompleteProps, AutocompleteOption } from "./Autocomplete.types";

import type { ElementType } from "react";

export type Size = "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl";

/**
 * What a navigation primitive owes a router.
 *
 * Every nav surface here — `Navbar.Item`, `Sidebar.Item`, `Menu.Item`,
 * `MobileMenu.Item`, `Breadcrumbs.Item` — used to hardcode a plain `<a href>`.
 * That is a FULL PAGE LOAD in every client-routed app, and the only way around
 * it was to nest a router `<Link>` inside the item: an anchor inside an anchor,
 * which is invalid HTML and the same nested-anchor shape that already cost this
 * suite an SSR hydration bug.
 *
 * `as` is the seam {@link ButtonProps.as} already had. It is router-agnostic on
 * purpose — one prop serves Inertia, TanStack Router, React Router and Next
 * rather than a package per router:
 *
 * ```tsx
 * // href-based routers (Inertia, Next)
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 *
 * // to-based routers (TanStack Router, React Router) — `to` reaches the Link
 * // through the forwarded rest props
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} to="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 * ```
 *
 * Link mode engages on `href` OR `as`, because a `to`-based router never passes
 * an `href` and would otherwise silently render the non-interactive fallback.
 */
export interface NavigableProps {
  /** Target URL. Renders link mode with a plain `<a>` unless `as` is given. */
  href?: string;
  /**
   * Link-mode element override — the component to render INSTEAD of the plain
   * `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link>` so navigation happens client-side. Receives
   * `className`, the item's `data-*` handles, and every unrecognized prop, so
   * router-specific props (`to`, `params`, `preload`, `search`) pass straight
   * through. Ignored in button mode.
   */
  as?: ElementType;
}

/**
 * The full Tailwind v4 named color palette — every default hue, including all
 * five gray families — plus `brand`, the host's own colour. Components that
 * accept a `color` should type it as this so the whole palette is available.
 *
 * `brand` is not a hue. It resolves through three CSS variables the host sets
 * once, rather than through a Tailwind scale:
 *
 *   `--color-brand`, `--color-brand-contrast`, `--color-brand-hover`
 *
 * Three rather than one because a generated hover assumes "same hue, darker",
 * and a brand palette need not work that way — navy whose hover is gold cannot
 * be derived from navy by any amount of arithmetic. The host states it.
 */
export type Color =
  // the host's own colour, resolved from CSS variables (see styles.css)
  | "brand"
  // grays
  | "slate"
  | "gray"
  | "zinc"
  | "neutral"
  | "stone"
  // hues
  | "red"
  | "orange"
  | "amber"
  | "yellow"
  | "lime"
  | "green"
  | "emerald"
  | "teal"
  | "cyan"
  | "sky"
  | "blue"
  | "indigo"
  | "violet"
  | "purple"
  | "fuchsia"
  | "pink"
  | "rose";

/** Every value of {@link Color}, for building exhaustive class maps. */
export const COLORS = [
  "brand",
  "slate", "gray", "zinc", "neutral", "stone",
  "red", "orange", "amber", "yellow", "lime", "green", "emerald", "teal",
  "cyan", "sky", "blue", "indigo", "violet", "purple", "fuchsia", "pink", "rose",
] as const satisfies readonly Color[];

export type Variant = "solid" | "outline" | "ghost" | "soft";

/** Button accepts the full Tailwind v4 palette (alias of {@link Color}). */
export type ButtonColor = Color;

/**
 * @deprecated Renamed to {@link ButtonColor}. `ActionColor` remains as an alias
 * for backward compatibility and will be removed in a future major version.
 */
export type ActionColor = ButtonColor;

export type Placement =
  | "top"
  | "bottom"
  | "left"
  | "right"
  | "top-start"
  | "top-end"
  | "bottom-start"
  | "bottom-end";

import type { ElementType } from "react";

export type Size = "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl";

/**
 * What a navigation primitive owes a router.
 *
 * Every nav surface here — `Navbar.Item`, `Sidebar.Item`, `Menu.Item`,
 * `MobileMenu.Item`, `Breadcrumbs.Item` — used to hardcode a plain `<a href>`.
 * That is a FULL PAGE LOAD in every client-routed app, and the only way around
 * it was to nest a router `<Link>` inside the item: an anchor inside an anchor,
 * which is invalid HTML and the same nested-anchor shape that already cost this
 * suite an SSR hydration bug.
 *
 * `as` is the seam {@link ButtonProps.as} already had. It is router-agnostic on
 * purpose — one prop serves Inertia, TanStack Router, React Router and Next
 * rather than a package per router:
 *
 * ```tsx
 * // href-based routers (Inertia, Next)
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 *
 * // to-based routers (TanStack Router, React Router) — `to` reaches the Link
 * // through the forwarded rest props
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} to="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 * ```
 *
 * Link mode engages on `href` OR `as`, because a `to`-based router never passes
 * an `href` and would otherwise silently render the non-interactive fallback.
 */
export interface NavigableProps {
  /** Target URL. Renders link mode with a plain `<a>` unless `as` is given. */
  href?: string;
  /**
   * Link-mode element override — the component to render INSTEAD of the plain
   * `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link>` so navigation happens client-side. Receives
   * `className`, the item's `data-*` handles, and every unrecognized prop, so
   * router-specific props (`to`, `params`, `preload`, `search`) pass straight
   * through. Ignored in button mode.
   */
  as?: ElementType;
}

/**
 * The full Tailwind v4 named color palette — every default hue, including all
 * five gray families — plus `brand`, the host's own colour. Components that
 * accept a `color` should type it as this so the whole palette is available.
 *
 * `brand` is not a hue. It resolves through three CSS variables the host sets
 * once, rather than through a Tailwind scale:
 *
 *   `--color-brand`, `--color-brand-contrast`, `--color-brand-hover`
 *
 * Three rather than one because a generated hover assumes "same hue, darker",
 * and a brand palette need not work that way — navy whose hover is gold cannot
 * be derived from navy by any amount of arithmetic. The host states it.
 */
export type Color =
  // the host's own colour, resolved from CSS variables (see styles.css)
  | "brand"
  // grays
  | "slate"
  | "gray"
  | "zinc"
  | "neutral"

  | "red"
  | "orange"
  | "amber"
  | "yellow"

files.content:
import { createContext, useContext } from "react";
import type { CardContextValue, CardPadding } from "./Card.types";

/**
 * What a Card tells its parts.
 *
 * `null` is a SUPPORTED state, not an error — unlike `useAccordion`, which
 * throws. `Card.Header` and `Card.Footer` are usable on their own, as a section
 * heading above a card, and before this existed they rendered with a
 * `border-bottom` belonging to a card they were not inside. So the absence of a
 * card is information: it means "style yourself standalone", and it is why this
 * hook returns the value rather than asserting it.
 */
export const CardContext = createContext<CardContextValue | null>(null);

export function useCardContext(): CardContextValue | null {
  return useContext(CardContext);
}

/**
 * The padding step of the section a child sits inside, or `null` when there is
 * no padded section above it.
 *
 * `Card.Bleed` needs it because escaping the padding is two different
 * operations depending on depth, and a component cannot see its own depth:
 *
 *   - Bleed inside a Header/Body/Footer is a GRANDchild of the card — the
 *     padding is on that section, and reaching the card's edge means a negative
 *     margin.
 *   - Bleed as a direct child of the card IS the padded element — the padding
 *     is on Bleed itself, and reaching the edge means zeroing it. A negative
 *     margin here would pull the content outside the card entirely.
 *
 * Both look like "cancel the padding" and neither works for the other case,
 * which is exactly the kind of thing that ships looking fine in one demo.
 *
 * It carries the STEP rather than a boolean because the step is the only thing
 * the bleed actually needs, and it is NOT always derivable from the card's
 * `size`: `<Card size="md" padding="lg">` pads its children by `lg`, and a
 * standalone `Card.Header` has a card-less step of its own. A boolean sent the
 * bleed back to `size` for the distance, which was wrong in both of those
 * cases — by a whole padding step, silently.
 */
export const CardSectionContext = createContext<CardPadding | null>(null);

export function useCardSectionPadding(): CardPadding | null {
  return useContext(CardSectionContext);
}

items.name: fancy-app-update
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-app-update
items.description: Framework-agnostic "a new version is available — refresh" detector for any React app — custom API, version compare, or zero-config ETag polling. No Inertia/PHP; self-contained prompt. fancy-inertia adds an Inertia-409 default on top.

items.name: fancy-artboard
items.title: fancy-artboard
items.description: Figma-style design canvas for Human+ UX — a pan/zoom board of image / HTML / live-JSX frames grouped into sections, with focus mode, drag-reorder, sticky notes, and PNG/HTML export.

items.name: fancy-auto-common
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-auto-common
items.description: Shared Human+ primitives — AgentActivity events, presence, undo stacks, and effect helpers. Low-level plumbing reused across the kit; usually installed transitively.

items.name: fancy-brand-icons
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-brand-icons
items.description: Brand-icon addendum for react-fancy — your logos + curated CC0 third-party marks (GitHub, X, Slack, Stripe, …) layered on top of any active icon set, so bare <Icon name="github"/> resolves the brand mark. Zero runtime deps; tree-shakeable.

items.name: fancy-catalog-js
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-catalog
items.description: Node/TS port of laravel-catalog — headless Stripe catalog (products / prices / plans + checkout), adapter-based with an injected Stripe client. Composes with @particle-academy/fancy-features for entitlements via its ./features bridge. No UI.

items.name: fancy-catalog-py
items.title: fancy-catalog
items.description: Python twin of laravel-catalog -- Stripe products, prices, plans and checkout, framework-free.

items.name: fancy-cf-relay
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-cf-relay
items.description: CDN-safe browser relay channel for agent-integrations' RelayTransport. Adaptive SSE↔long-poll with Cloudflare detection, so the MCP relay survives a Cloudflare/HTTP-3 edge that resets long-lived SSE streams. Zero runtime deps.

items.name: fancy-cli
items.title: fancy-cli
items.description: Source-vendoring CLI — `npx fancy-cli@latest add <component>` copies component source from the registry into your project (the shadcn-style own-the-source path).

items.name: fancy-cms
items.title: particle-academy/fancy-cms
items.description: Laravel host + PHP page renderer for the Stages doc model: node tree → HTML with island hydration; backend pair of the fancy-cms-ui editor. Pre-1.0 — the API may still move between minors; issues at github.com/Particle-Academy/fancy-cms/issues.

items.name: fancy-conformance
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-conformance
items.description: Shared cross-language fixture tables, so parity between a PHP twin and its Node/Python siblings is a TEST RESULT rather than a claim in a README.

items.name: fancy-connector-core
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-connector-core
items.description: The connector runtime: typed delivery, failure classification (unreachable / refused / ambiguous / rejected), retries, and sandbox-vs-live selection. Every connector is built on it.

items.name: fancy-diff
items.title: FancyDiff
items.description: Controlled split / inline diff viewer; per-hunk accept/reject with a merged result, render-prop customization, and a git unified-diff datasource.

items.name: fancy-doc-commons
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-doc-commons
items.description: Shared pure core for the Fancy document/surface packages — the model an agent or human emits and edits. Flat node-tree + collab-safe fractional ordering, a typed op-spine contract (reduce + invert), an infinite-canvas primitive, and a surface-agnostic staged-write (accept/reject) model. Zero dependencies, no React.

items.name: fancy-features-js
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-features
items.description: Node/TS port of laravel-fms — headless, framework-agnostic gating of features, access and metered quotas for any app: gate / registry / config / group strategies. Owns the FeatureSource contract that @particle-academy/fancy-catalog plugs INTO. No UI.

items.name: fancy-features-py
items.title: fancy-features
items.description: Python twin of laravel-fms -- gate features, access and metered resources in any app, framework-free. Same FeatureSource contract as the PHP and Node siblings; commerce is one consumer of it, not a requirement.

items.name: fancy-file-commons
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-file-commons
items.description: Shared pure core for the file-focused packages (editors / viewers / writers / diff surfaces) — the structured diff engine + model, git unified-diff parser, merge resolution, per-line gutter annotations, path helpers, and filename→language. Zero deps, no React; fancy-diff re-exports it and the fancy-code diff gutter runs on it.

items.name: fancy-flow
items.title: fancy-flow
items.description: Headless workflow engine + an optional React Flow editor — built-in trigger, logic, data, AI, human-in-the-loop and terminal nodes, a topological executor, and a FlowRunnerUx flow→UX bridge. The editor designs graphs; `/engine` runs them with zero React on a server, worker, or CLI (runtime twins: fancy-flow-php, fancy-flow-py).

items.name: fancy-flow-mcp
items.title: particle-academy/fancy-flow-mcp
items.description: A Laravel MCP server that lets an agent build fancy-flow workflows HEADLESSLY -- list node kinds, add and connect nodes, configure them, validate and export a WorkflowSchema, without a canvas. Wraps fancy-flow-php, so the graph an agent composes here is the same document <FlowEditor> opens and the same one the PHP, TypeScript and Python runtimes execute.

items.name: fancy-flow-mcp-js
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-flow-mcp-js
items.description: The Node twin of fancy-flow-mcp -- an MCP server that lets an agent build fancy-flow workflows HEADLESSLY on a TypeScript host: list node kinds, add and connect nodes, configure them, validate and export a WorkflowSchema, without a canvas. Same 15 tools as the PHP twin, name for name, asserted by a test that reads them out of the PHP source rather than mirroring them.

items.name: fancy-flow-php
items.title: particle-academy/fancy-flow-php
items.description: PHP runtime for fancy-flow workflow graphs — the framework-free twin of @particle-academy/fancy-flow's engine. Same WorkflowSchema JSON in, same outputs out; author in <FlowEditor>, run on PHP. Adds a Laravel layer: queued durable runs with resume-from-checkpoint, human approval + user_input pauses, and an agent node. Headless; no UI.

items.name: fancy-flow-py
items.title: fancy-flow
items.description: Python runtime twin of the fancy-flow engine -- the same graph, the same node kinds, durable and queued runs. Pairs with fancy-flow (TS) and fancy-flow-php.

items.name: fancy-grid

items.name: fancy-heuristics
items.title: particle-academy/fancy-heuristics

items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-heuristics-js

items.name: fancy-mlm
items.title: particle-academy/fancy-mlm
items.description: Framework-agnostic multi-level referral / network-marketing engine — configurable unilevel / binary / matrix downlines, level decay + tier multipliers, dynamic compression. Pure-PHP core with an optional Laravel bridge + fun-lab / catalog / fms integration. Headless; pairs with @particle-academy/fancy-mlm-ui.

items.name: fancy-mlm-js
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-mlm
items.description: Node/TS mirror of particle-academy/fancy-mlm — the same CompensationPlan JSON + unilevel / binary / matrix trees yield identical rewards, isomorphic (browser or Node). Headless; no UI.

items.name: fancy-passkeys
items.title: particle-academy/fancy-passkeys
items.description: Passkey (WebAuthn) login for PHP — registration + authentication ceremonies, discoverable (usernameless) credentials, single-use server-side challenges, clone detection via the signature counter, and a Laravel bridge that augments Fortify rather than replacing it. A thin wrapper over web-auth/webauthn-lib: no cryptography of our own. Headless; pairs with @particle-academy/fancy-passkeys-ui.

items.name: fancy-passkeys-js
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-passkeys
items.description: Node/TS mirror of particle-academy/fancy-passkeys — the same four-endpoint wire contract, byte-compatible options payloads (pinned by shared fixtures), and the same challenge / counter / redaction policy, so one React UI works against either backend. Wraps @simplewebauthn/server. Headless; framework-free with a dependency-free HTTP adapter.

items.name: fancy-pixel
items.title: fancy-pixel

items.name: fancy-ws
items.title: @particle-academy/fancy-ws
items.description: ZERO-DEPENDENCY WebSocket SERVER for Node — RFC 6455 framing over node:http's `upgrade` event, on node:http/net/crypto/events and nothing else. Node 22 ships a WebSocket CLIENT (the `WebSocket` global, from undici) and no server; this is the other half. `verify` runs BEFORE the 101, so a refused handshake is a plain HTTP 401/403 rather than an accept-then-close that hands an unauthenticated peer a live frame parser.

export { Field } from "./Field";
export type { FieldProps } from "./Field.types";

import type { ElementType } from "react";

export type Size = "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl";

/**
 * What a navigation primitive owes a router.
 *
 * Every nav surface here — `Navbar.Item`, `Sidebar.Item`, `Menu.Item`,
 * `MobileMenu.Item`, `Breadcrumbs.Item` — used to hardcode a plain `<a href>`.
 * That is a FULL PAGE LOAD in every client-routed app, and the only way around
 * it was to nest a router `<Link>` inside the item: an anchor inside an anchor,
 * which is invalid HTML and the same nested-anchor shape that already cost this
 * suite an SSR hydration bug.
 *
 * `as` is the seam {@link ButtonProps.as} already had. It is router-agnostic on
 * purpose — one prop serves Inertia, TanStack Router, React Router and Next
 * rather than a package per router:
 *
 * ```tsx
 * // href-based routers (Inertia, Next)
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 *
 * // to-based routers (TanStack Router, React Router) — `to` reaches the Link
 * // through the forwarded rest props
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} to="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 * ```
 *
 * Link mode engages on `href` OR `as`, because a `to`-based router never passes
 * an `href` and would otherwise silently render the non-interactive fallback.
 */
export interface NavigableProps {
  /** Target URL. Renders link mode with a plain `<a>` unless `as` is given. */
  href?: string;
  /**
   * Link-mode element override — the component to render INSTEAD of the plain
   * `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link>` so navigation happens client-side. Receives
   * `className`, the item's `data-*` handles, and every unrecognized prop, so
   * router-specific props (`to`, `params`, `preload`, `search`) pass straight
   * through. Ignored in button mode.
   */
  as?: ElementType;
}

/**
 * The full Tailwind v4 named color palette — every default hue, including all
 * five gray families — plus `brand`, the host's own colour. Components that
 * accept a `color` should type it as this so the whole palette is available.
 *
 * `brand` is not a hue. It resolves through three CSS variables the host sets
 * once, rather than through a Tailwind scale:
 *
 *   `--color-brand`, `--color-brand-contrast`, `--color-brand-hover`
 *
 * Three rather than one because a generated hover assumes "same hue, darker",
 * and a brand palette need not work that way — navy whose hover is gold cannot
 * be derived from navy by any amount of arithmetic. The host states it.
 */
export type Color =
  // the host's own colour, resolved from CSS variables (see styles.css)
  | "brand"
  // grays
  | "slate"
  | "gray"
  | "zinc"
  | "neutral"
  | "stone"
  // hues
  | "red"
  | "orange"
  | "amber"
  | "yellow"
  | "lime"
  | "green"
  | "emerald"
  | "teal"
  | "cyan"
  | "sky"
  | "blue"
  | "indigo"
  | "violet"
  | "purple"
  | "fuchsia"
  | "pink"
  | "rose";

/** Every value of {@link Color}, for building exhaustive class maps. */
export const COLORS = [
  "brand",
  "slate", "gray", "zinc", "neutral", "stone",
  "red", "orange", "amber", "yellow", "lime", "green", "emerald", "teal",
  "cyan", "sky", "blue", "indigo", "violet", "purple", "fuchsia", "pink", "rose",
] as const satisfies readonly Color[];

export type Variant = "solid" | "outline" | "ghost" | "soft";

/** Button accepts the full Tailwind v4 palette (alias of {@link Color}). */
export type ButtonColor = Color;

/**
 * @deprecated Renamed to {@link ButtonColor}. `ActionColor` remains as an alias
 * for backward compatibility and will be removed in a future major version.
 */
export type ActionColor = ButtonColor;

export type Placement =
  | "top"
  | "bottom"
  | "left"
  | "right"
  | "top-start"
  | "top-end"
  | "bottom-start"
  | "bottom-end";

import type { ElementType } from "react";

export type Size = "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl";

/**
 * What a navigation primitive owes a router.
 *
 * Every nav surface here — `Navbar.Item`, `Sidebar.Item`, `Menu.Item`,
 * `MobileMenu.Item`, `Breadcrumbs.Item` — used to hardcode a plain `<a href>`.
 * That is a FULL PAGE LOAD in every client-routed app, and the only way around
 * it was to nest a router `<Link>` inside the item: an anchor inside an anchor,
 * which is invalid HTML and the same nested-anchor shape that already cost this
 * suite an SSR hydration bug.
 *
 * `as` is the seam {@link ButtonProps.as} already had. It is router-agnostic on
 * purpose — one prop serves Inertia, TanStack Router, React Router and Next
 * rather than a package per router:
 *
 * ```tsx
 * // href-based routers (Inertia, Next)
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 *
 * // to-based routers (TanStack Router, React Router) — `to` reaches the Link
 * // through the forwarded rest props
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} to="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 * ```
 *
 * Link mode engages on `href` OR `as`, because a `to`-based router never passes
 * an `href` and would otherwise silently render the non-interactive fallback.
 */
export interface NavigableProps {
  /** Target URL. Renders link mode with a plain `<a>` unless `as` is given. */
  href?: string;
  /**
   * Link-mode element override — the component to render INSTEAD of the plain
   * `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link>` so navigation happens client-side. Receives
   * `className`, the item's `data-*` handles, and every unrecognized prop, so
   * router-specific props (`to`, `params`, `preload`, `search`) pass straight
   * through. Ignored in button mode.
   */
  as?: ElementType;
}

/**
 * The full Tailwind v4 named color palette — every default hue, including all
 * five gray families — plus `brand`, the host's own colour. Components that
 * accept a `color` should type it as this so the whole palette is available.
 *
 * `brand` is not a hue. It resolves through three CSS variables the host sets
 * once, rather than through a Tailwind scale:
 *
 *   `--color-brand`, `--color-brand-contrast`, `--color-brand-hover`
 *
 * Three rather than one because a generated hover assumes "same hue, darker",
 * and a brand palette need not work that way — navy whose hover is gold cannot
 * be derived from navy by any amount of arithmetic. The host states it.
 */
export type Color =
  // the host's own colour, resolved from CSS variables (see styles.css)
  | "brand"
  // grays
  | "slate"
  | "gray"
  | "zinc"
  | "neutral"
  | "stone"
  // hues
  | "red"
  | "orange"
  | "amber"
  | "yellow"
  | "lime"
  | "green"
  | "emerald"
  | "teal"
  | "cyan"
  | "sky"
  | "blue"
  | "indigo"
  | "violet"
  | "purple"
  | "fuchsia"
  | "pink"
  | "rose";

/** Every value of {@link Color}, for building exhaustive class maps. */
export const COLORS = [
  "brand",
  "slate", "gray", "zinc", "neutral", "stone",
  "red", "orange", "amber", "yellow", "lime", "green", "emerald", "teal",
  "cyan", "sky", "blue", "indigo", "violet", "purple", "fuchsia", "pink", "rose",
] as const satisfies readonly Color[];

export type Variant = "solid" | "outline" | "ghost" | "soft";

/** Button accepts the full Tailwind v4 palette (alias of {@link Color}). */
export type ButtonColor = Color;

/**
 * @deprecated Renamed to {@link ButtonColor}. `ActionColor` remains as an alias
 * for backward compatibility and will be removed in a future major version.
 */
export type ActionColor = ButtonColor;

export type Placement =
  | "top"
  | "bottom"
  | "left"
  | "right"
  | "top-start"
  | "top-end"
  | "bottom-start"
  | "bottom-end";

items.name: menu
items.title: Menu
items.description: Menu from react-fancy

files.content:
import type { ElementType } from "react";

export type Size = "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl";

/**
 * What a navigation primitive owes a router.
 *
 * Every nav surface here — `Navbar.Item`, `Sidebar.Item`, `Menu.Item`,
 * `MobileMenu.Item`, `Breadcrumbs.Item` — used to hardcode a plain `<a href>`.
 * That is a FULL PAGE LOAD in every client-routed app, and the only way around
 * it was to nest a router `<Link>` inside the item: an anchor inside an anchor,
 * which is invalid HTML and the same nested-anchor shape that already cost this
 * suite an SSR hydration bug.
 *
 * `as` is the seam {@link ButtonProps.as} already had. It is router-agnostic on
 * purpose — one prop serves Inertia, TanStack Router, React Router and Next
 * rather than a package per router:
 *
 * ```tsx
 * // href-based routers (Inertia, Next)

files.content:
import type { SVGAttributes } from "react";

import type { QrErrorCorrection, QrMode } from "./qr-encode";

export type { QrErrorCorrection, QrMode };

/**
 * `viewBox` is omitted because the component computes it from the symbol's
 * module count — overriding it would rescale the modules and break the
 * crispness the vector output exists for.
 *
 * `version` is omitted because SVG has an attribute of that name and ours
 * means the QR symbol version, a number. SVG's is a no-op in SVG 2 and was
 * only ever a document-conformance hint, so nothing is lost by shadowing it,
 * where renaming our prop would cost the one word every QR reference uses.
 */
export interface QrCodeProps
  extends Omit<SVGAttributes<SVGSVGElement>, "children" | "viewBox" | "version"> {
  /**
   * What the code carries. **Any string** — this is not a link component.
   *
   * A QR code is a byte container, and most of what goes in one is not a web
   * address: a serial or asset number, a batch or lot code, a ticket or order
   * id, a WiFi credential block (`WIFI:T:WPA;S:ssid;P:pass;;`), a contact card
   * (vCard / MeCard), a `tel:` / `mailto:` / `geo:` URI, a shipment code, a
   * bare numeric reference, or arbitrary text. Several of those are the cases
   * where a QR code earns its place, because they work with no network at all.
   *
   * The encoder picks the narrowest mode the value allows, so a digits-only
   * value is a third of the size it would be as text — see {@link mode}.
   *
   * An empty string renders a valid (empty) symbol rather than throwing, so a
   * controlled surface can render before its value arrives.
   */
  value: string;
  /** Rendered width and height in pixels. Default 192. */
  size?: number;
  /**
   * Error correction level. Default `"M"` — about 15% of the symbol can be
   * damaged and still read, which is the usual choice for a screen.
   *
   * Higher is not better by default: `"H"` survives ~30% damage and holds a
   * third less, so the same value needs a bigger symbol with smaller modules,
   * and on a phone screen that can read WORSE than `"M"` at the same pixel
   * size. Raise it for print, for a label that will be scuffed, or when a logo
   * covers part of the symbol.
   */
  errorCorrection?: QrErrorCorrection;
  /**
   * Accessible name. **Required**, and it must describe WHAT THE CODE IS FOR
   * rather than the artefact: "Asset tag for pump 14" or "Join the guest WiFi"
   * tells a screen-reader user something useful, where "QR code" tells them
   * only that an image they cannot use is present.
   *
   * It is not a substitute for the value being available another way. A QR code
   * is unusable by anyone who cannot point a second device at this screen, so
   * the value should also appear as selectable text nearby — the `aria-label`
   * cannot carry a serial number or a password someone is expected to read off.
   */
  label: string;
  /**
   * Modules of quiet zone around the symbol. Default 4, which is the
   * standard's minimum.
   *
   * **Do not set this to 0 to save space.** The quiet zone is not padding; it
   * is how a scanner finds the symbol's edge. A code flush against
   * surrounding content is the single most common reason a QR code that looks
   * perfect will not scan.
   */
  quietZone?: number;
  /** Module colour. Default `currentColor`, so it inherits text colour. */
  foreground?: string;
  /**
   * Background colour. Default `"transparent"`.
   *
   * **A transparent background inherits whatever is behind it**, so on a dark
   * surface the symbol renders dark-on-dark and most scanners will not read
   * it. Set an explicit light background, or set `foreground` and background
   * together, when the surface is not light. Contrast is what gets scanned,
   * not the dark modules on their own.
   */
  background?: string;
  /**
   * Force a mode instead of picking the narrowest that fits. Rarely useful;
   * the default packs digits three to ten bits where byte mode spends 24.
   */
  mode?: QrMode;
  /**
   * Force a symbol version (1–40), fixing the module count regardless of how
   * little the value needs. Useful when several codes must render at the same
   * module scale. Throws if the value does not fit.
   */
  version?: number;
}

export { RadioGroup } from "./RadioGroup";
export type { RadioGroupProps } from "./RadioGroup.types";

import type { ElementType } from "react";

export type Size = "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl";

/**
 * What a navigation primitive owes a router.
 *
 * Every nav surface here — `Navbar.Item`, `Sidebar.Item`, `Menu.Item`,
 * `MobileMenu.Item`, `Breadcrumbs.Item` — used to hardcode a plain `<a href>`.
 * That is a FULL PAGE LOAD in every client-routed app, and the only way around
 * it was to nest a router `<Link>` inside the item: an anchor inside an anchor,
 * which is invalid HTML and the same nested-anchor shape that already cost this
 * suite an SSR hydration bug.
 *
 * `as` is the seam {@link ButtonProps.as} already had. It is router-agnostic on
 * purpose — one prop serves Inertia, TanStack Router, React Router and Next
 * rather than a package per router:
 *
 * ```tsx
 * // href-based routers (Inertia, Next)
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 *
 * // to-based routers (TanStack Router, React Router) — `to` reaches the Link
 * // through the forwarded rest props
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} to="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 * ```
 *
 * Link mode engages on `href` OR `as`, because a `to`-based router never passes
 * an `href` and would otherwise silently render the non-interactive fallback.
 */
export interface NavigableProps {
  /** Target URL. Renders link mode with a plain `<a>` unless `as` is given. */
  href?: string;
  /**
   * Link-mode element override — the component to render INSTEAD of the plain
   * `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link>` so navigation happens client-side. Receives
   * `className`, the item's `data-*` handles, and every unrecognized prop, so
   * router-specific props (`to`, `params`, `preload`, `search`) pass straight
   * through. Ignored in button mode.
   */
  as?: ElementType;
}

/**
 * The full Tailwind v4 named color palette — every default hue, including all
 * five gray families — plus `brand`, the host's own colour. Components that
 * accept a `color` should type it as this so the whole palette is available.
 *
 * `brand` is not a hue. It resolves through three CSS variables the host sets
 * once, rather than through a Tailwind scale:
 *
 *   `--color-brand`, `--color-brand-contrast`, `--color-brand-hover`
 *
 * Three rather than one because a generated hover assumes "same hue, darker",
 * and a brand palette need not work that way — navy whose hover is gold cannot
 * be derived from navy by any amount of arithmetic. The host states it.
 */
export type Color =
  // the host's own colour, resolved from CSS variables (see styles.css)
  | "brand"
  // grays
  | "slate"
  | "gray"
  | "zinc"
  | "neutral"
  | "stone"
  // hues
  | "red"
  | "orange"
  | "amber"
  | "yellow"
  | "lime"
  | "green"
  | "emerald"
  | "teal"
  | "cyan"
  | "sky"
  | "blue"
  | "indigo"
  | "violet"
  | "purple"
  | "fuchsia"
  | "pink"
  | "rose";

/** Every value of {@link Color}, for building exhaustive class maps. */
export const COLORS = [
  "brand",
  "slate", "gray", "zinc", "neutral", "stone",
  "red", "orange", "amber", "yellow", "lime", "green", "emerald", "teal",
  "cyan", "sky", "blue", "indigo", "violet", "purple", "fuchsia", "pink", "rose",
] as const satisfies readonly Color[];

export type Variant = "solid" | "outline" | "ghost" | "soft";

/** Button accepts the full Tailwind v4 palette (alias of {@link Color}). */
export type ButtonColor = Color;

/**
 * @deprecated Renamed to {@link ButtonColor}. `ActionColor` remains as an alias
 * for backward compatibility and will be removed in a future major version.
 */
export type ActionColor = ButtonColor;

export type Placement =
  | "top"
  | "bottom"
  | "left"
  | "right"
  | "top-start"
  | "top-end"
  | "bottom-start"
  | "bottom-end";

export { Select } from "./Select";

import type { ElementType } from "react";

export type Size = "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl";

/**
 * What a navigation primitive owes a router.
 *
 * Every nav surface here — `Navbar.Item`, `Sidebar.Item`, `Menu.Item`,
 * `MobileMenu.Item`, `Breadcrumbs.Item` — used to hardcode a plain `<a href>`.
 * That is a FULL PAGE LOAD in every client-routed app, and the only way around
 * it was to nest a router `<Link>` inside the item: an anchor inside an anchor,
 * which is invalid HTML and the same nested-anchor shape that already cost this
 * suite an SSR hydration bug.
 *
 * `as` is the seam {@link ButtonProps.as} already had. It is router-agnostic on
 * purpose — one prop serves Inertia, TanStack Router, React Router and Next
 * rather than a package per router:
 *
 * ```tsx
 * // href-based routers (Inertia, Next)
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 *
 * // to-based routers (TanStack Router, React Router) — `to` reaches the Link
 * // through the forwarded rest props
 * <Navbar.Item as={Link} to="/dashboard">Dashboard</Navbar.Item>
 * ```
 *
 * Link mode engages on `href` OR `as`, because a `to`-based router never passes
 * an `href` and would otherwise silently render the non-interactive fallback.
 */
export interface NavigableProps {
  /** Target URL. Renders link mode with a plain `<a>` unless `as` is given. */
  href?: string;
  /**
   * Link-mode element override — the component to render INSTEAD of the plain
   * `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link>` so navigation happens client-side. Receives
   * `className`, the item's `data-*` handles, and every unrecognized prop, so
   * router-specific props (`to`, `params`, `preload`, `search`) pass straight
   * through. Ignored in button mode.
   */
  as?: ElementType;
}

/**
 * The full Tailwind v4 named color palette — every default hue, including all
 * five gray families — plus `brand`, the host's own colour. Components that
 * accept a `color` should type it as this so the whole palette is available.
 *
 * `brand` is not a hue. It resolves through three CSS variables the host sets
 * once, rather than through a Tailwind scale:
 *
 *   `--color-brand`, `--color-brand-contrast`, `--color-brand-hover`
 *
 * Three rather than one because a generated hover assumes "same hue, darker",
 * and a brand palette need not work that way — navy whose hover is gold cannot
 * be derived from navy by any amount of arithmetic. The host states it.
 */
export type Color =
  // the host's own colour, resolved from CSS variables (see styles.css)
  | "brand"
  // grays
  | "slate"
  | "gray"
  | "zinc"
  | "neutral"
  | "stone"
  // hues
  | "red"
  | "orange"
  | "amber"
  | "yellow"
  | "lime"
  | "green"
  | "emerald"
  | "teal"
  | "cyan"
  | "sky"
  | "blue"
  | "indigo"
  | "violet"
  | "purple"
  | "fuchsia"
  | "pink"
  | "rose";

/** Every value of {@link Color}, for building exhaustive class maps. */
export const COLORS = [
  "brand",
  "slate", "gray", "zinc", "neutral", "stone",
  "red", "orange", "amber", "yellow", "lime", "green", "emerald", "teal",
  "cyan", "sky", "blue", "indigo", "violet", "purple", "fuchsia", "pink", "rose",
] as const satisfies readonly Color[];

export type Variant = "solid" | "outline" | "ghost" | "soft";

/** Button accepts the full Tailwind v4 palette (alias of {@link Color}). */
export type ButtonColor = Color;

/**
 * @deprecated Renamed to {@link ButtonColor}. `ActionColor` remains as an alias
 * for backward compatibility and will be removed in a future major version.
 */
export type ActionColor = ButtonColor;

export type Placement =
  | "top"
  | "bottom"
  | "left"
  | "right"
  | "top-start"
  | "top-end"
  | "bottom-start"
  | "bottom-end";

files.content:
import type { EditorAction } from "@particle-academy/react-fancy"; /** * Presentation-tuned toolbar preset for the react-fancy `Editor` used to edit * slide text inline. Only commands that round-trip cleanly through the editor's * `htmlToMarkdown` output are included — bold (`**`), italic (`*`), heading * (`## `), and bullet list (`- `). Box-level typography (alignment, color, font * size, line height) is NOT here: those are per-element `TextStyle` properties * edited in the ElementInspector, and `text-align`/color spans don't survive the * markdown the slide content commits to. */ export const PRESENTATION_EDITOR_ACTIONS: EditorAction[] = [ { icon: "B", label: "Bold", command: "bold" }, { icon: "I", label: "Italic", command: "italic" }, { icon: "H", label: "Heading", command: "formatBlock", commandArg: "

" }, { icon: "P", label: "Paragraph", command: "formatBlock", commandArg: "

" }, { icon: "•", label: "Bullet list", command: "insertUnorderedList" }, ]; /** * Normalize the `Editor`'s markdown output to the *line-based* paragraph model * the slide content commits to. The editor emits a blank line (`\n\n`) between * `

` blocks, but `splitParagraphs` (and the dark-slide pptx writer) treat a * single `\n` as one paragraph / build unit, and a blank interior line as its * own (phantom) build. Collapsing runs of newlines to a single `\n` keeps * "by paragraph" reveals and per-paragraph pptx builds correct — bullets are * already one-per-`\n`, so they're unaffected. The round-trip invariant * (`content → Editor → normalize → content` preserves the `\n` paragraph count) * is covered by a unit test. */ export function normalizeSlideMarkdown(md: string): string { return md .replace(/\r\n/g, "\n") .replace(/\n{2,}/g, "\n") .replace(/[ \t]+$/gm, "") .trim(); }

 * Link mode engages on `href` OR `as`, because a `to`-based router never passes
 * an `href` and would otherwise silently render the non-interactive fallback.
 */
export interface NavigableProps {
  /** Target URL. Renders link mode with a plain `<a>` unless `as` is given. */
  href?: string;
  /**
   * Link-mode element override — the component to render INSTEAD of the plain
   * `<a>`, e.g. a router's `<Link>` so navigation happens client-side. Receives
   * `className`, the item's `data-*` handles, and every unrecognized prop, so
   * router-specific props (`to`, `params`, `preload`, `search`) pass straight
   * through. Ignored in button mode.
   */
  as?: ElementType;
}

/**
 * The full Tailwind v4 named color palette — every default hue, including all
 * five gray families — plus `brand`, the host's own colour. Components that
 * accept a `color` should type it as this so the whole palette is available.
 *
 * `brand` is not a hue. It resolves through three CSS variables the host sets
 * once, rather than through a Tailwind scale:
 *
 *   `--color-brand`, `--color-brand-contrast`, `--color-brand-hover`
 *
 * Three rather than one because a generated hover assumes "same hue, darker",
 * and a brand palette need not work that way — navy whose hover is gold cannot
 * be derived from navy by any amount of arithmetic. The host states it.
 */
export type Color =
  // the host's own colour, resolved from CSS variables (see styles.css)
  | "brand"
  // grays
  | "slate"
  | "gray"
  | "zinc"
  | "neutral"
  | "stone"
  // hues
  | "red"
  | "orange"
  | "amber"
  | "yellow"
  | "lime"
  | "green"
  | "emerald"
  | "teal"
  | "cyan"
  | "sky"
  | "blue"
  | "indigo"
  | "violet"
  | "purple"
  | "fuchsia"
  | "pink"
  | "rose";

/** Every value of {@link Color}, for building exhaustive class maps. */
export const COLORS = [
  "brand",
  "slate", "gray", "zinc", "neutral", "stone",
  "red", "orange", "amber", "yellow", "lime", "green", "emerald", "teal",
  "cyan", "sky", "blue", "indigo", "violet", "purple", "fuchsia", "pink", "rose",
] as const satisfies readonly Color[];

export type Variant = "solid" | "outline" | "ghost" | "soft";

/** Button accepts the full Tailwind v4 palette (alias of {@link Color}). */
export type ButtonColor = Color;

/**
 * @deprecated Renamed to {@link ButtonColor}. `ActionColor` remains as an alias
 * for backward compatibility and will be removed in a future major version.
 */
export type ActionColor = ButtonColor;

export type Placement =
  | "top"
  | "bottom"
  | "left"
  | "right"
  | "top-start"
  | "top-end"
  | "bottom-start"
  | "bottom-end";
